newsitem.title: UK: China world's top market for frozen foods--report.
newsitem.headline: China world's top market for frozen foods--report.

text.p: China became the world's leading market for frozen foods in 1996, overtaking the U.S. as rising disposable income and an increasing taste for Western convenience foods propels growth, a market research group reported on Monday.

China in 1996 accounted for consumption of 3.8 million tonnes of frozen foods, Euromonitor said in its report, "The World Market for Frozen Foods." The U.S., however, remains the largest frozen food market based on monetary value, with 1996 sales of $15.9 billion. China and the U.S. together represent about 43 percent of worldwide frozen food consumption in volume terms, followed by the UK, Euromonitor said.
China is expected to increase its consumption of frozen foods to 6.1 million tonnes by the year 2001, Euromonitor said.

On a per capita basis, frozen food consumption in China remains low by Western standards and is concentrated in the frozen fruit sector. Denmark, by contrast, has the highest per capita consumption of frozen foods at 37 kilograms per person. Britain ranks as the country where frozen food accounts for the highest proportion of total food consumption at nine percent, Euromonitor said.
